title: Amarnath Yatra Resumes After Six-Day Weather Halt as Monsoon Recedes in Kashmir
excerpt: Pilgrims set off from the Baltal and Nunwan base camps on Friday after heavy rainfall, landslides and eight flood deaths had shut both routes since July 19.
body:
• The Amarnath Yatra resumed on Friday after a six-day suspension caused by heavy monsoon rainfall, landslides and shooting stones along the high-altitude routes.
  • Both the Pahalgam and Baltal routes were reopened after weather conditions improved and authorities completed safety assessments.
  • The suspension, ordered on July 19, came after the India Meteorological Department issued a severe weather warning for the region. At least eight people died in monsoon-related incidents across Jammu division during the halt.
  • Over 3.7 lakh pilgrims have visited the holy cave shrine since the yatra began on July 3, with the pilgrimage scheduled to conclude on August 28.

Routes Reopen After Monsoon Fury

Fresh batches of pilgrims departed for the Amarnath cave shrine from both the Nunwan and Baltal base camps on Friday morning, ending a six-day halt that had stranded thousands of devotees at transit camps across Jammu and Kashmir.

Divisional Commissioner Kashmir Anshul Garg had ordered the suspension on July 19 as a precautionary measure after the India Meteorological Department issued a severe weather warning. Continuous rainfall triggered landslides and shooting stones at several vulnerable points along the mountainous routes, making passage dangerous.

"Over 3.7 lakh pilgrims have visited the holy cave shrine since the yatra began on July 3, with the pilgrimage scheduled to conclude on August 28."

Eight Dead in Monsoon-Related Incidents

The weather that shut the pilgrimage also brought devastation to the wider Jammu region. At least eight people were killed in monsoon-related incidents, including landslides and flash floods. The Shri Shiv Khori pilgrimage in the Ransoo area was also suspended during the same period.

The annual 57-day Amarnath Yatra began on July 3 and is scheduled to conclude on August 28. The pilgrimage to the holy cave shrine, situated at 3,888 metres above sea level in the Kashmir Himalayas, is one of Hinduism's most important journeys. Weather-related interruptions during the monsoon season are not uncommon, but a six-day continuous halt is among the longest in recent years.

Strong Turnout Despite Disruptions

More than 3.7 lakh pilgrims have paid obeisance at the holy cave shrine since the yatra began, a pace that officials say is on track with recent years despite the weather disruption. The area beyond the base camps has been declared a no-fly zone for security reasons, meaning no helicopter service is available to pilgrims this year.

Planning Tips for NRI Pilgrims

NRIs planning to undertake the Amarnath Yatra should monitor weather advisories closely. Registration is mandatory for pilgrims between the ages of 13 and 70. The monsoon season, which typically peaks in July and August, regularly causes route closures. Travel insurance covering weather-related delays and medical emergencies is strongly recommended for the high-altitude trek.
